messages:
maria: :rotating_light: NA-west2 control plane auth proxy losing TTL sync, console sessions failing for ~8m. Seeing 502s on console and /v1/auth calls timing out.
aj: Confirmed 502s from console in na-west2, token refreshes failing. User sessions stuck on stale cookies.
kevin: Noted increased 5xxs on routing-proxy, dropping KV sync for auth-keys. Metrics spike in `auth_proxy_sync_failures`.
sophie: tagging @ops-oncall — can we failover console/auth to na-central and redirect traffic?
ops-oncall: On it. Initiating traffic shift policy to prefer na-central for console and auth. Will run graceful conn drain for na-west2 proxies.
infra-bot: Automated rollback of recent config rollout attempt detected at 1798765400 — config ttl-sync toggle was enabled. Rolling back now.
paul: Was there a canary? I see a partial rollout to na-west2 that toggled `auth.session_ttl_sync`.
maria: Yes, last deploy toggled TTL sync change in 2 clusters. Post-deploy we saw replication lag. Suspect config change exposed an existing race in ephemeral session propagation.
aj: Executing reroute: `sh /opt/redwood/scripts/shift-traffic.sh --from na-west2 --to na-central --services console,auth-proxy`
kevin: Watch logs: `kubectl logs -l app=auth-proxy -n prod --tail=100` — seeing `ERROR session: ttl mismatch for token id=...` repeated.
sophie: After starting shift, console 200s increased in na-central. But some API keys still hitting na-west2 due to DNS cache TTL.
ops-oncall: Flushing internal region DNS cache and expiring route caches: `curl -X POST https://infra-api/regions/na-west2/route-cache/flush`
infra-bot: Route cache flush accepted.
paul: Spawning emergency GPU workers in na-central for Dedicated capacity? Hmm cost tradeoff if we move inference workloads during auth failover. Do we need it now?
aj: Not for auth path — this is control plane / console. But note: some inference traffic uses console-managed tokens; if we prolong shift, we might need to scale capacity to keep throughput.
maria: Current priority: restore management plane (console/auth) so customers can control Dedicated fleets. Defer large GPU moves unless telemetry shows customer jobs failing.
kevin: Brief check: `netstat` shows sustained TCP connections to na-west2 auth backends. Connection draining in progress.
sophie: Customer comms: posting banner to status page and in-app message for affected regions. Draft: "We are experiencing partial console access interruptions in na-west2. We are routing traffic to na-central and investigating; no model inference impact expected"
ops-oncall: Update: traffic shift hitting 85% success to na-central for auth calls. Console 502s dropping but still ~3% errors.
paul: Any suspected underlying infra issue beyond config toggle? Disk pressure or etcd lag?\maria: Etcd metrics show minor election latency during rollout time, but not full cluster partition. Likely propagation bug in our session replication layer when TTL sync enabled concurrently with rolling update.
kevin: Captured sample logs for debugging:
```
time=2026-04-02T10:05:12Z level=error component=auth_proxy msg="session ttl mismatch" token=abc123 src=10.2.4.7
time=2026-04-02T10:05:12Z level=warn component=sync-worker msg="kv apply delayed" key=auth/sessions/ttl
```
maria: Root cause hypothesis: `auth.session_ttl_sync` flag enabled during a rolling rollout causing out-of-order TTL updates; leads to token rejection on some proxies.
sophie: Next steps: 1) complete rollback of the TTL sync flag; 2) finish traffic shift to na-central; 3) re-run controlled canary with improved guard (check kv-lag < 50ms).
ops-oncall: Rollback completed at 1798766000. Monitoring auth success rate.
infra-bot: Canary guard check added to deploy pipeline: `kv_lag_threshold_ms=50` for session-related flags.
aj: I've paused all config rollouts touching auth/session until patch is out.
kevin: Will add extra logging and a small fix to serialize TTL updates — PR opened: `github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4721`
paul: Quick cost note — shifting long-lived traffic to na-central increases egress in some topologies; finance ping if we keep shift >6h.
maria: Agreed — ops to monitor and provide estimate if shift continues. For now, focus on stability.
sophie: Status update for channel and postmortem owners: please assign someone for RCA and customer impact timeline. I can take customer comms.
ops-oncall: Assigning RCA to kevin + maria. Postmortem template will be started.
kevin: Current metrics: auth success rate back to 99.6% globally, na-west2 errors <0.5%. Will keep observing for 2h before closing incident.
maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees console errors re-open thread.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline paused for auth flags until approval by infra leads."
